channel.title: ipe() Games Journal
channel.description: The ipe() Games journal: notes on turn-based games, killing-time games and the philosophy behind our short-round games.

item.title: One new rule at a time
item.description: A different way to raise difficulty in a game for spare minutes, and how our games approach their own learning curves.

item.title: Three ways to claim land
item.description: Why 'make this part of the board mine' is such a durable shape, and how Iltonggi, Inkisle and Claimball each use it.

item.title: Losing a short round
item.description: What a loss costs in a game for spare minutes, and the difference between losing and being cheated.

item.title: Pick a game by how much attention you have
item.description: Four spare-minute situations, and which of our four games is built for each. None is out yet, so this is a guide to intent.

item.title: A board you can read at a glance
item.description: Reading who owns what without effort: the small design choices that make a quick game legible.

item.title: A game for one hand
item.description: Designing for the moments when one hand holds a bag, a rail or a cup, and what Inkisle does about it.

item.title: An opponent to practice against
item.description: What we want from an AI opponent in a game for spare minutes, and how Claimball's rivals are meant to work.

item.title: One tub for two players
item.description: What changes when you and your opponent build in the same space, and how Sunmeld's shared tub puts it on one screen.

item.title: The first round is a welcome
item.description: Why the opening round of a strategy game should be smaller than the rest, and how Iltonggi shapes its first one.

item.title: The part of the map you cannot see
item.description: What fog adds to a turn-based game, where it can go wrong, and how Iltonggi uses it.

item.title: A good time-killer does not kill time
item.description: Four conditions for a game that lets you rest instead of just passing the time, and how ipe() games try to meet them.

item.title: Why turn-based games fit a break
item.description: Why a game where the world waits for your move suits a few spare minutes, and where ipe() games fit.

item.title: How ipe makes games
item.description: The five principles behind ipe() games, and where each of our four games keeps them. The first post in this journal.
